questions.explain: Exfiltration is an outbound connection, so an egress allowlist stops it. Inbound TLS and inbound allowlists protect who reaches the agent, not where it can send data, and rate limits do not restrict destinations.

questions.stem: Two internal microservices exchange data with a model-serving service. The security team requires that both the client and server cryptographically prove their identities on every connection. What should be implemented?
options: Static API keys in request headers
questions.explain: mTLS has both sides present certificates, authenticating client and server. One-way TLS authenticates only the server, API keys are bearer secrets rather than mutual cryptographic proof, and rate limiting is not authentication.

questions.stem: A mobile app calls an LLM API using a provider API key compiled into the app. What is the MAIN problem with this design?
options: The key can be extracted from the app and abused by anyone
It prevents the use of TLS
questions.explain: Secrets embedded in client code can be extracted, letting attackers call the API at your cost. Calls should go through a backend or gateway that holds credentials and authenticates users. The other options are not consequences of this design.

questions.case: A company runs a model inference cluster and a vector database in the cloud. Both currently have public IP addresses and accept connections from anywhere with a valid API key. Internal apps are the only legitimate consumers.
questions.stem: Which TWO changes BEST reduce the network attack surface? (Select TWO.)
options: Move both services to private endpoints on a segmented internal network
Expose only an authenticated API gateway to the internal apps
Publish the API keys in an internal wiki so apps can find them
Increase the vector database's storage capacity
questions.explain: Private endpoints with segmentation remove internet exposure, and a single authenticated gateway becomes the controlled entry point. Publishing keys, adding storage and disabling logging do not reduce attack surface and some increase risk.

questions.stem: An agent's outbound network policy is defined in JSON. Complete the policy so the agent may connect only to the listed domains and everything else is blocked.
questions.explain: An allowlist works only when the default action is deny, so anything not explicitly listed is blocked. A default of allow or log would permit exfiltration to arbitrary destinations, and redirect is not a blocking control.

questions.stem: For each statement about network and API access for AI systems, select Yes if true.

statements.s: OAuth 2.0 access tokens with limited scopes are generally preferred over long-lived shared API keys.
Encrypting traffic with TLS is sufficient on its own to authenticate who is calling the API.
Code-execution sandboxes used by agents should have no network access unless it is explicitly required.

questions.explain: Scoped, expiring tokens limit damage if stolen. Standard TLS encrypts and authenticates the server but not the caller. Default-deny networking for sandboxes limits exfiltration and SSRF.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a permission-aware RAG request in order.
options: The user authenticates and submits a question
The retriever searches the vector store using the user's identity
Results are filtered to documents the user is authorized to read
Only authorized passages are added to the prompt
The model generates an answer from the authorized context
questions.explain: Authorization is applied during retrieval, before any content enters the prompt, so the model never sees documents the user could not open directly.

questions.stem: A mobile app sends customer prompts to a hosted LLM API over the internet. Which control protects the prompts from interception on the network?
options: TLS 1.2 or later on the connection to the API endpoint
AES-256 encryption of the vector database volumes
Dynamic data masking applied to the model's responses
A trusted execution environment on the inference server
questions.explain: Data crossing a network is in transit, so TLS is the control. Volume encryption protects stored data at rest. Masking changes what viewers see but does not encrypt traffic. A TEE protects data in use during processing, not on the wire.

questions.stem: A team is hardening a RAG system. Which TWO controls address encryption at rest? Select TWO.
options: Encrypt the vector database storage with keys held in a KMS
Enable mutual TLS between the orchestrator and the vector database
Encrypt snapshots and backups of the embedding store
Run the embedding model inside a confidential VM
Mask personal data in prompts before they are embedded
questions.explain: Encrypting the vector store and its backups protects stored data at rest. mTLS protects data in transit. A confidential VM protects data in use. Masking is a data safety technique, not encryption.

questions.case: A credit union stores its fine-tuning datasets and model weights in cloud object storage. They are encrypted with provider-managed keys. A new regulation requires the credit union itself to control key rotation and to be able to make the data unreadable immediately if the provider relationship ends.
questions.stem: Which change best meets the requirement?
options: Upgrade all API connections to TLS 1.3
Tokenize the customer identifiers in the datasets
Use customer-managed keys in a KMS or HSM with a defined rotation policy
Enable dynamic data masking on the storage bucket
questions.explain: Customer-managed keys give the organization control of rotation and revocation; revoking the key makes the data unreadable. TLS protects data in transit only. Tokenization protects some fields but not weights. Masking changes views, not key ownership.

questions.stem: Which technology protects prompts and model weights while they are being processed in memory, even from the cloud host's administrators?
options: Full-disk encryption on the inference servers
TLS termination at the API gateway
Salted hashing of every prompt before inference
questions.explain: A TEE keeps memory encrypted and isolated during processing, which is encryption in use. Disk encryption covers data at rest. TLS covers data in transit and ends at the gateway. Hashing is one-way, so a hashed prompt could not be processed by the model.

questions.stem: For each statement about encryption in use, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Homomorphic encryption allows computation on encrypted data without first decrypting it.
Encryption at rest protects model weights while they are loaded in GPU memory for inference.
Remote attestation lets a client verify that an enclave is genuine before it sends sensitive data.

questions.explain: Homomorphic encryption computes on ciphertext. Data at rest is decrypted when loaded into memory, so encryption at rest no longer protects it there; that is the job of a TEE. Attestation proves the TEE and its code before data or keys are released.

questions.stem: A company wants to stop documents marked as HR-Confidential from being indexed into the knowledge base of a chatbot that all employees use. Which control is the best fit?
options: A response confidence threshold on the chatbot
Data classification labels enforced by the ingestion pipeline
Per-user rate limits on the chatbot API
Static masking of the chatbot's conversation logs
questions.explain: Classification labels let the ingestion pipeline automatically exclude HR-Confidential documents from the general index. Confidence thresholds address answer quality. Rate limits address volume abuse. Masking logs does nothing to stop the documents from being indexed and retrieved.

questions.stem: A developer's prompt for drafting delivery-delay apologies includes the customer's full profile: address, date of birth, payment history and support tickets. Only the first name, order number and new delivery date are needed. Which principle should the developer apply?
questions.explain: Data minimization means sending only the data the task needs, which is just the three fields. Anonymization would remove the first name the apology needs. Augmentation and balancing are training-data techniques for adding or evening out samples, not privacy controls for prompts.

questions.stem: Which technique transforms personal data so that individuals can no longer be identified and the change cannot be reversed?
questions.explain: Anonymization is irreversible. Pseudonymization and tokenization keep a mapping that can re-identify people, so the data is still personal data. Dynamic masking hides values from some viewers but leaves the original stored.

questions.stem: Support agents reviewing AI chat transcripts should see only the last four digits of customer account numbers, while an authorized fraud team must still see the full values in the same records. Which technique fits?
options: Redaction of account numbers before storage
Data minimization in the chatbot prompt
Dynamic data masking based on the viewer's role
questions.explain: Dynamic masking changes what each role sees at query time while the stored value stays intact for authorized users. Redaction and anonymization remove the values permanently, so the fraud team would lose them. Minimization would stop the data being collected at all.

questions.case: A health provider will fine-tune a model on clinical notes to suggest discharge summaries. Analysts do not need patient identities. The privacy officer worries the model could memorize and later repeat patient names and medical record numbers.
questions.stem: Which TWO actions best reduce this risk? Select TWO.
options: Encrypt the training dataset at rest and train on it unchanged
Redact direct identifiers such as names and record numbers before training
Apply dynamic masking in the clinicians' user interface
Generalize quasi-identifiers such as exact dates and ages before training
Increase the number of training epochs
questions.explain: Removing identifiers and generalizing quasi-identifiers before training means the model never learns them. Encryption at rest does not change what the model learns. UI masking does not affect training. More epochs increase overfitting and memorization.

questions.stem: A team logs and inspects only the prompts users type into its AI assistant. Which issue are they most likely to miss?
options: A user submitting an unusually long prompt
The model disclosing sensitive data in reply to a harmless-looking question
A user sending prompts from a new IP address
A spike in the number of prompts sent by one user
questions.explain: Leaks show up in the response, so only response monitoring catches them when the query looks benign. Prompt length, source IP and prompt volume are all visible from the query side and gateway metadata.

questions.stem: Which TWO indicators are best detected by monitoring the query (input) side of an LLM application? Select TWO.
options: Prompts asking the model to disregard its earlier instructions
A response that contains text from the hidden system prompt
An increase in average response latency
Prompts containing long encoded or obfuscated text blocks
Higher GPU utilization on the inference cluster
questions.explain: Override requests and obfuscated blocks are visible in the input. System prompt text in a reply is a response-side finding. Latency and GPU utilization are performance metrics, not prompt content.

questions.stem: For each statement about prompt monitoring, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Response monitoring can detect system prompt leakage even when the triggering query looked harmless.
Only the user's typed text needs inspection; retrieved RAG documents can be trusted.
Prompt and response detections should be sent to a SIEM for correlation with other events.

questions.explain: Leaks appear in outputs regardless of how the query looked. Retrieved content is a key route for indirect prompt injection, so it must be inspected too. A SIEM lets AI events be correlated with identity and network logs.

questions.stem: An investigator needs to know which tools an AI agent invoked, and with what parameters, during an incident. Which log source is most useful?
options: Web server access logs for the chat front end
Firewall flow logs for the inference subnet
questions.explain: Tool-call logs record each tool, its parameters and its results. Web server logs show page requests, not tool invocations. Training curves describe model learning. Flow logs show connections but not which tool ran or with what arguments.

questions.case: AI gateway logs show that one partner's API key, normally used from a single data centre, made requests from IP addresses in 37 countries within an hour. Prompt content looks like ordinary product questions, and the partner says it changed nothing.
questions.stem: What is the most likely explanation, and what should the SOC do first?
options: The API key was leaked or shared; revoke and rotate it, then investigate
The model is hallucinating; lower the temperature setting
The training data was poisoned; roll back to the previous model
The prompt template is misconfigured; restore the previous template
questions.explain: A key used from many new locations points to credential compromise, so revoke and rotate it and investigate. Hallucination concerns answer accuracy, not caller location. Poisoning would show in model behaviour. A template fault would not change where requests come from.

questions.stem: You are setting up log monitoring for a new LLM application. Put the steps in order.
options: Identify log sources such as the gateway, app, agent tools and vector database
Normalize the logs and forward them to the central SIEM
Establish baselines and write detection rules
Alert, triage and respond to detections
Tune rules based on findings and false positives
questions.explain: You must know the sources before you can collect them. Logs must be centralized before you can baseline them. Rules must exist before they can alert, and tuning uses what was learned from real alerts.

questions.stem: Before writing chatbot prompts and responses to its log store, an application replaces email addresses, API keys and card numbers with placeholders. What is this practice called?
questions.explain: Removing or replacing sensitive values before logging is sanitization. Protection secures logs after they are written (encryption, immutability, access control). Rotation manages file size and age. Aggregation collects logs centrally.

questions.stem: Complete the Python function so it replaces US Social Security numbers in a prompt with a placeholder before the prompt is logged.
questions.explain: re.sub replaces every match of the pattern with the replacement string and returns the new text. re.match only tests the start of the string, re.findall returns the matches themselves, and re.split breaks the text apart; none of them redacts.

questions.stem: Analysts notice fake entries in an AI application's text logs, such as an approval record that never happened. The fake lines came from a user prompt that contained embedded line-break characters. Which control addresses this?
options: Increase the log retention period to one year
Encode or strip CR/LF control characters in prompt text before logging
Encrypt the log files at rest
questions.explain: This is log injection, and sanitizing control characters before writing stops forged lines. Retention and encryption do not change what is written. Dropping response logs does not help, because the fake lines came from the prompt, and it would remove useful evidence.

questions.stem: An attacker who gains admin rights on an AI application should not be able to erase its audit trail. Which TWO controls best achieve this? Select TWO.
options: Reduce log verbosity to limit what an attacker could change
Keep logs on the application server for fast access
Send logs to append-only (WORM) immutable storage
Sanitize personal data from logs before writing
Store logs in a separate security account that app admins cannot modify
questions.explain: Immutable storage and separation of duties stop app admins from deleting or changing logs. Lower verbosity loses evidence. Keeping logs on the app server puts them within the attacker's reach. Sanitization protects privacy, not log integrity.

questions.stem: For each statement about protecting AI logs, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Hashing or hash chaining of log records helps detect tampering.
Once prompts are sanitized, AI logs no longer need access controls.
Log retention should align with legal, regulatory and investigation requirements.

questions.explain: Hash chains reveal edits. Sanitized logs still reveal user behaviour, system details and evidence, so they still need access control. Retention should meet legal and investigation needs without keeping data longer than necessary.

questions.stem: A fraud model returns a score of 0.52 for a transaction. The system automatically sends any prediction scored below 0.80 to a human analyst. What does this describe?
options: Rate limiting on the inference API
A response confidence threshold with human review
Model pruning to remove low-value weights
questions.explain: Routing low-confidence predictions to people is a confidence threshold with human-in-the-loop review. Rate limiting controls request volume. Pruning shrinks the model. Output encoding makes output safe to insert into HTML, SQL or other contexts.

questions.stem: A public image classification API returns the full probability for every class with six decimal places. The security team is worried about model extraction and model inversion. Which change reduces the risk while keeping the service useful?
options: Compress the full probability vector before returning it
Publish the model architecture so callers can calibrate the scores
Return only the top label or a coarse, rounded confidence band
Raise per-user quotas so legitimate users are not throttled
questions.explain: Precise probability vectors give attackers rich signals for extraction and inversion, so returning less detail reduces risk while still answering the caller. Compression returns the same information. Publishing the architecture helps attackers. Higher quotas allow more probing.

questions.stem: Complete the SQL query so it returns only API keys that sent more than 500 requests in the last hour.
questions.code:
SELECT api_key_id, COUNT(*) AS requests
FROM llm_requests
WHERE request_time > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
GROUP BY api_key_id
____ COUNT(*) > 500;
questions.explain: HAVING filters groups after aggregation, so it can test COUNT(*). WHERE filters rows before grouping and is not allowed after GROUP BY. ORDER BY sorts rather than filters. LIMIT caps the number of rows and needs a number, not a condition.

questions.stem: Rate dashboards show one account sending a steady three requests per second around the clock. The inputs systematically vary across the feature range, and every response's scores are stored. What is the most likely activity?
options: A hallucination problem in the model
Data poisoning of the training pipeline
questions.explain: Systematic, high-volume querying that collects outputs is the classic sign of model extraction. Hallucination is an accuracy problem. Log injection forges log entries. Poisoning requires changing training data, not querying the inference API.

questions.stem: An AI assistant's monthly bill tripled. The number of prompts stayed flat, but the average answer length rose from about 200 to 1,500 tokens after a prompt change. Which cost category grew?
options: Storage costs for the vector database
questions.explain: Longer answers mean more output tokens, which are billed per token and often at a higher rate than input. Storage and fine-tuning did not change. The request count stayed flat, so more prompts is not the cause.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI cost monitoring, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Vector database and log storage are part of AI cost monitoring, not just token charges.
A denial-of-wallet attack aims to drive up an organization's AI usage costs.
Setting a maximum output token limit has no effect on response costs.

questions.explain: Storage is one of the four cost areas. Denial of wallet abuses pay-per-use billing. Capping output tokens directly limits response cost per request.

questions.case: A budget alert fires after an AI agent spends 80% of its monthly budget in two days. Traces show the agent retrying a failing tool hundreds of times per task and sending the entire conversation history with each retry.
questions.stem: Which control best limits this cost exposure?
options: Move the agent to a larger model with a bigger context window
Disable prompt logging to reduce storage costs
Cap agent iterations per task and enforce hard spending limits with alerts
Anonymize the conversation history before each retry
questions.explain: Iteration caps stop runaway loops, and hard spending limits contain the damage while the tool is fixed. A larger model or context window raises cost. Logging is a small share of spend and is needed as evidence. Anonymizing does not reduce token volume.

questions.stem: A legal research assistant uses RAG to cite case law. Which audit method best measures its hallucination rate?
options: Track average GPU utilization per response
Sample responses and verify each claim and citation against the source documents
Count the tokens in each response and flag long answers
Confirm that all API calls use TLS 1.2 or later
questions.explain: Hallucination audits check whether outputs are supported by the sources, including whether citations exist and say what is claimed. GPU use, token counts and TLS versions are operational or security metrics that say nothing about factual accuracy.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a recurring accuracy and hallucination audit in order.
options: Define accuracy metrics and acceptable thresholds
Build a ground-truth test set with verified answers
Evaluate test-set and sampled production responses against verified sources
Record findings and compare them with thresholds and previous audits
questions.explain: You need metrics and thresholds before you can judge results, and a verified test set before you can evaluate. Findings are compared with thresholds, and only then can remediation be targeted and re-tested.

questions.case: A lender's pre-screening model does not use ethnicity as an input. A quarterly audit finds approval rates differ by 20 percentage points between postcode areas, and those areas correlate strongly with ethnicity.
questions.stem: Which TWO audit actions are most appropriate? Select TWO.
options: Raise the confidence threshold for every applicant
Measure fairness metrics such as approval-rate differences across protected groups
Investigate postcode and similar features as proxies for protected attributes
Stop logging decisions to protect applicant privacy
Close the finding because ethnicity is not a model input
questions.explain: Fairness metrics quantify the disparity, and proxy analysis finds its cause. A blanket threshold change does not address bias. Removing logs destroys audit evidence. Leaving out the protected attribute does not prove fairness when proxies carry the same signal.

questions.stem: For each statement about auditing AI systems, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Access audits should review which users, service accounts and agents can use a model or its data, and remove access that is no longer needed.
A bias audit performed once before deployment is sufficient for the life of the model.
Compliance audits may require logs showing who accessed a model and when.

questions.explain: Access reviews enforce least privilege for people, services and agents. Bias can appear after retraining or drift, so audits recur. Access logs are standard compliance evidence.

questions.stem: A help-desk assistant starts following instructions hidden in a customer-uploaded PDF. Which attack does this evidence indicate?
questions.explain: Instructions arriving inside processed content are indirect prompt injection.

questions.stem: Which compensating control separates fixed developer instructions from user-supplied data in each request?
questions.explain: Prompt templates keep instructions and user data in defined slots, making injection harder.

questions.stem: Logs show many requests rephrased through role-play and encodings until the safety filter stops triggering. What is this?
questions.explain: Iterating phrasing to slip past filters is guardrail circumvention.

questions.stem: Which compensating control inspects prompts and responses at a gateway in front of the model?
questions.explain: A prompt firewall sits inline and filters inputs and outputs.

questions.stem: After a fine-tuning run on crowd-sourced labels, a classifier consistently misclassifies one vendor's invoices as low risk. What is the most likely attack?
questions.explain: Corrupted training labels causing targeted misbehaviour is data poisoning.

questions.stem: A hiring model's recommendations shift against one demographic after attacker-influenced training data was added. Which attack is this?
questions.explain: Poisoning aimed at skewing outcomes against a group is introducing bias.

questions.stem: Which compensating control best detects tampering with training datasets before they are used?
options: Data integrity controls such as hashes and signed dataset versions
questions.explain: Integrity checks reveal unauthorised changes to data.

questions.stem: Small, nearly invisible changes to images make a vision model misclassify them. What is this attack?
questions.explain: Crafted perturbations at inference time are evasion or adversarial examples.

questions.stem: An attacker abuses an AI assistant's connector to a ticketing system to create and close tickets at will. Which attack category fits?
questions.explain: Abusing the connectors around the model is integration manipulation.

questions.stem: A model confidently cites a law that doesn't exist, and staff act on it. Which TWO issues does this combine?
questions.explain: False confident output is hallucination; acting on it without checking is overreliance.

questions.stem: An attacker queries a medical model repeatedly and reconstructs features of patients in its training set. Which attack is this?
questions.explain: Reconstructing training data features from outputs is model inversion.

questions.stem: Which mitigation most directly reduces both inversion and membership inference risk?
options: Reducing output detail (no raw confidence scores) and applying differential privacy
questions.explain: Less output detail and differential privacy limit what can be inferred about individual records.

questions.stem: An API shows one account issuing millions of systematic queries, and a near-identical competitor model appears soon after. What is the likely attack?
questions.explain: Training a copy from large volumes of API answers is model extraction, a form of model theft.

questions.stem: Which TWO compensating controls reduce model theft risk? (Select TWO)
options: Publishing the weights to a public repository
Disabling authentication for ease of use
Rate limiting and query monitoring on the inference API
Access controls and encryption for model files in registries and storage
questions.explain: Rate limits slow extraction; access control and encryption protect weight files.

questions.stem: A team fine-tunes a downloaded pretrained model, and the result contains a hidden trigger the team never trained. Which attack fits?
options: Transfer learning attack via a backdoored base model
questions.explain: Backdoors in a pretrained base model carry over into fine-tuned models.

questions.stem: A popular ML library on a package registry is replaced with a malicious version that exfiltrates training data. What is this?
questions.explain: Compromising third-party components you build on is a supply chain attack.

questions.stem: Attackers flood a recommendation system's feedback channel with fake ratings so the continuously trained model drifts in their favour. What is this?
questions.explain: Manipulating ongoing learning data so predictions drift is model skewing.

questions.stem: Fraud scores are altered in transit between the model and the payments system. Which attack, and which control?
options: Output integrity attack; sign or hash results and use authenticated, encrypted channels
questions.explain: Tampering with results after inference is an output integrity attack; integrity checks and secure channels address it.

questions.stem: Model output containing script tags runs in users' browsers. Which attack is this?
questions.explain: Passing unvalidated output to a browser enables XSS: insecure output handling.

questions.stem: A plug-in accepts a free-text 'query' that is passed straight to a SQL database. Which weakness does this show?
questions.explain: Plug-ins should take strictly typed, validated parameters with least privilege.

questions.stem: Users submit extremely long, recursive prompts that max out context and spike costs. Which attack is this?
questions.explain: Resource-exhausting requests are model DoS.

questions.stem: Which TWO compensating controls address model DoS? (Select TWO)
options: Rate limiting per user and per API key
Maximum input and output token limits
questions.explain: Rate and token limits cap resource use.

questions.stem: A chatbot reveals another customer's order history. Which cause should the analyst check FIRST?
options: Retrieval or tools running without per-user access controls
questions.explain: Cross-user disclosure usually means missing per-user access control on data sources.

questions.stem: An AI agent with full admin rights deletes production resources after misreading a request. Which weakness is primary, and the fix?
options: Excessive agency; least privilege and human approval for destructive actions
questions.explain: Too much permission and autonomy turned an error into damage.

questions.stem: For each pairing, select Yes if the compensating control fits the attack.

statements.s: Prompt injection → prompt firewall plus prompt templates
Model DoS → rate limiting and token caps
Model theft from storage → prompt templates

questions.explain: Prompt-layer controls fit injection; rate limits fit DoS; stolen weight files need access control and encryption.

questions.stem: For each pairing, select Yes if the compensating control fits the attack.

statements.s: Training data tampering → data integrity controls
Excessive agency → least privilege
Membership inference → larger output detail

questions.explain: Integrity checks detect tampering; least privilege limits agency; more output detail makes inference easier.

questions.stem: Order the analyst's workflow for an AI incident.
options: Review the evidence in logs and outputs
questions.explain: Analyse evidence, classify the attack, choose controls, then implement and verify.

questions.stem: Which control best protects model weights and embeddings stored in object storage?
options: Encryption at rest with strict access controls on keys and buckets
questions.explain: Encryption and access control protect stored artefacts.

questions.stem: Case: a customer bot has been jailbroken, flooded with costly prompts, and leaks its system prompt containing an API key. Which TWO controls address the MOST issues at once? (Select TWO)
options: A prompt firewall/guardrail layer inspecting inputs and outputs
Publishing the API key so it isn't secret
questions.explain: A firewall/guardrail layer addresses jailbreak and leakage attempts; rate and token limits address DoS. The key must also be rotated and moved out of the prompt.

questions.stem: For each scenario, select Yes if it describes overreliance.

statements.s: Analysts paste AI-generated firewall rules into production without review
A reviewer checks AI-drafted code against tests before merging
Managers accept AI risk scores as final without any human validation

questions.explain: Overreliance is trusting outputs without verification; review and testing counter it.

questions.stem: A model trained on unsanitised support tickets reproduces customers' phone numbers. Which control should have prevented this?
options: Sanitising and minimising training data (PII removal) before training
questions.explain: PII in training data can be memorised and regurgitated; sanitise it first.

questions.stem: Case: an AI coding assistant's output is executed by a CI pipeline without review, and one suggestion opens a reverse shell. Which TWO weaknesses combine here?
questions.explain: Executing model output unvalidated (insecure output handling) and trusting it without review (overreliance).

questions.stem: A development team wants AI to flag hard-coded secrets and injection-prone code while developers are typing, before the code is committed. Which tool type BEST fits?
questions.explain: An IDE plug-in runs inside the code editor and reviews code as it is written. A browser plug-in works on web pages, a CLI plug-in works in the terminal, and a personal assistant acts across mail, calendar and files.

questions.stem: A junior administrator uses an AI CLI plug-in that suggests a command to clean up disk space on a production server. What should the administrator do FIRST?
options: Run the command immediately because the plug-in is approved
Run the command with elevated privileges to make sure it completes
Review and understand the suggested command before executing it
Paste the command into a public chatbot to confirm it
questions.explain: AI suggestions can be wrong or destructive, so a human must review and understand them before running them. Approval of the tool doesn't make each suggestion safe, elevating privileges increases the blast radius, and public chatbots can leak data and are no more reliable.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI plug-ins, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An IDE plug-in may send source code to an external model, so data handling must be reviewed before approval.
A browser plug-in inherits no access to the content the user is viewing.
Using only sanctioned plug-ins helps reduce shadow AI risk.

questions.explain: Plug-ins send their host's context (code, page content) to a model, so data handling matters. Browser plug-ins can read the pages being viewed. Allowing only sanctioned plug-ins limits unmanaged shadow AI.

questions.stem: Which open standard lets an AI application connect to external tools, data resources and prompt templates through a common client-server protocol?
questions.explain: MCP standardizes how AI hosts connect, through clients, to servers that expose tools, resources and prompts. RAG is a grounding technique, not a protocol. OpenAPI describes REST APIs, and SAML is a federation standard for authentication.

questions.stem: Which of the following can an MCP server expose to an AI application? Select THREE.
questions.explain: MCP servers expose tools (callable actions), resources (readable data) and prompts (templates). They don't distribute model weights or manage GPU scheduling.

questions.case: A SOC lead wants analysts to query the SIEM and open tickets from an AI assistant. An engineer finds a community MCP server that does both. Its setup guide recommends a SIEM administrator API key and automatic approval of all tool calls.
questions.stem: Which change BEST reduces the risk before deployment?
options: Keep the admin key but rotate it monthly
Use a scoped, least-privilege credential and require user approval for write actions such as ticket creation
Expose the MCP server publicly so the vendor can patch it faster
Replace the MCP server with a browser plug-in that has the same key
questions.explain: Least-privilege credentials and human approval of sensitive tool calls limit the damage from a malicious server, a manipulated server or prompt injection. Rotating an admin key keeps excessive privilege in place, public exposure widens the attack surface, and a plug-in holding the same key has the same problem.

questions.stem: An executive's AI personal assistant can read and send email, edit calendar entries and open shared files. Whose permissions does the assistant effectively operate with?
questions.explain: Personal assistants act on the user's behalf with that user's delegated access. That makes their reach, and the risk of excessive agency, as broad as the user's access. They don't run as the provider, as a guest or as another analyst.

questions.stem: Which detection approach is MOST likely to identify a previously unseen threat that has no known indicators?
options: Anomaly detection against a behavioral baseline
questions.explain: Anomaly detection flags deviations from normal behavior, so it can catch threats that have no signature. Hashes, blocklists and definition updates all depend on threats that are already known.

questions.stem: A security team must block a specific known malware family with the FEWEST false positives. Which approach is BEST?
questions.explain: For a known threat, signature matching is precise and low-noise. Clustering and UEBA are better at unknowns but generate more false positives, and summarization is not a detection method.

questions.stem: An ML model notices that 300 phishing emails sent to different departments share the same HTML structure and sending cadence, even though their subjects differ. Which AI capability does this describe?
questions.explain: Spotting a recurring structure across many varied items, here one campaign, is pattern recognition. Signature matching needs a fixed known indicator, and translation and data minimization are unrelated.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI-based detection, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Anomaly detection often uses unsupervised learning because labeled attack data is scarce.
Signature matching reliably detects modified variants of malware it has never seen.
Anomaly detection typically produces more false positives than signature matching and needs tuning.

questions.explain: Unsupervised anomaly detection doesn't need labels, but it raises more false positives and needs tuning. Signatures miss variants that change the matched indicators.

questions.stem: A vulnerability scanner returned 4,000 findings. Which AI-assisted approach BEST helps the team decide what to fix first?
options: Sort findings strictly by CVSS base score
Fix findings in the order the scanner reported them
Prioritize by exploitability, exposure and asset criticality, with duplicates grouped
Suppress all findings older than 30 days
questions.explain: Risk-based prioritization combines exploitability, internet exposure and asset value, and grouping duplicates reduces the volume. CVSS alone ignores context, scanner order is arbitrary, and suppressing findings by age hides real risk.

questions.stem: A company plans to use an AI-driven automated penetration testing platform. Which controls are required before testing begins? Select THREE.
options: Written authorization and rules of engagement
A defined scope of approved targets and time windows
Human oversight with the ability to stop testing
Disabling logging on target systems to avoid noise
Granting the tool domain administrator rights by default
questions.explain: Automated pentesting needs authorization, a defined scope and human supervision. Disabling logging destroys evidence and visibility, and default domain admin rights break least privilege.

questions.stem: What does a linter primarily do?
options: Checks code against rules for errors, style issues and risky constructs
Generates software bills of materials from container registries
questions.explain: Linting is static rule-based checking of code, and AI linters add explanations and suggested fixes. Encryption, deployment and SBOM generation are separate functions.

questions.stem: An AI pentest assistant reports a critical remote code execution flaw in an internal web app, but the report cites a library version that the app doesn't use. What is the BEST next step?
options: Publish the finding to leadership immediately
Ignore all AI findings from now on
Manually validate the finding before reporting it, treating it as a possible hallucination
questions.explain: AI findings are leads that a human tester must confirm, and a wrong version suggests a hallucination. Publishing unverified results misleads leadership, discarding every AI finding wastes the tool, and an outage is premature.

questions.stem: An architect asks an AI assistant to list threats for a new API by category: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service and Elevation of privilege. Which framework is being applied?
questions.explain: Those six categories form STRIDE. DREAD scores risk, MITRE ATLAS catalogs adversary techniques against AI systems, and the OWASP LLM Top 10 lists LLM application risks.

questions.stem: A bank's AI fraud model gives a transaction a medium risk score. The bank wants to stop fraud without frustrating legitimate customers. Which response is BEST?
options: Trigger step-up authentication for the customer
Approve it and delete the score
Block all transactions from that country
questions.explain: A graduated response fits a medium score: step-up verification stops fraud while letting real customers continue. Closing the account or blocking a whole country is excessive, and ignoring the score defeats the model.

questions.stem: Which tasks can an AI copilot appropriately perform during incident management? Select TWO.
options: Correlate related alerts into a single incident
Enrich indicators with reputation and asset-owner context
Make final legal breach-notification decisions without review
Permanently delete evidence to save storage
questions.explain: Correlation and enrichment are typical AI assists. Legal notification decisions need accountable humans, and deleting evidence breaks forensics and chain of custody.

questions.case: Six months after deployment, an online retailer's fraud model approves more fraudulent orders while its false-positive rate stays flat. The fraud team reports that criminals have shifted to small, gift-card-heavy baskets that are rare in the training data.
questions.stem: What is the MOST appropriate action?
options: Raise the block threshold to approve more orders
Retrain the model with recent labeled fraud data and monitor for drift
Replace the model with static signature rules only
Disable the model until the next annual review
questions.explain: Fraud patterns drift, and retraining on recent labeled cases with ongoing drift monitoring restores detection. Raising the threshold makes the miss rate worse, static rules can't adapt, and disabling the model removes protection entirely.

questions.stem: Which type of summarization writes new sentences rather than copying them from the source, and is therefore more prone to hallucination?
questions.explain: Abstractive summaries paraphrase in new words, which reads well but can add unsupported facts. Extractive summaries copy source sentences, while indexing and tokenization aren't summarization methods.

questions.stem: An analyst uses AI to summarize a 70-page threat report for the CISO, including IP addresses and actor names. What is the MOST important step before sending it?
options: Increase the model temperature for richer wording
Remove all links to the source report
Translate it into a second language
Verify indicators and key facts against the original report
questions.explain: Summaries can drop or invent details, so a human must check critical facts against the source. A higher temperature increases variability, removing source links prevents verification, and translation adds nothing here.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI translation and summarization in security operations, select Yes if true.

statements.s: LLM translation can help analysts read foreign-language threat intelligence and phishing lures.
A document being summarized can contain hidden instructions that attempt prompt injection.
Pasting confidential incident data into any public chatbot is acceptable if the output is only a summary.

questions.explain: Translation widens intelligence coverage, and documents are an indirect prompt-injection channel. Sending confidential data to unsanctioned public tools risks leakage whatever the output is.

questions.stem: Employees share a fake news clip about their company believing it is true. Which term BEST describes this?
questions.explain: Misinformation is false content spread without intent to deceive, and these employees believe the clip. Disinformation needs deliberate deception, impersonation means pretending to be someone, and pretexting is a social engineering scenario.

questions.stem: A finance clerk receives a video call from someone who looks and sounds exactly like the CFO, requesting an urgent, confidential wire transfer. Which control is MOST effective?
options: Deploy a deepfake detection plug-in on the clerk's laptop only
Require stronger passwords for the finance team
Enforce call-back verification to a known number plus dual approval for transfers
questions.explain: Process controls such as out-of-band verification and dual approval work however convincing the deepfake is. Detection tools can be fooled, passwords don't address the scam, and banning video conferencing disrupts the business without fixing the process.

questions.stem: A help desk receives a voice call from an "executive" asking for an urgent MFA reset. The voice may be cloned. Put the steps in order.
options: Pause the request and do not act on the call alone
Call the executive back on the number held in the directory
Verify identity using the approved verification procedure
Perform the reset only if verification succeeds and log the event
questions.explain: Stop first, then verify out of band using a trusted number and the approved procedure, and act only after verification, logging what was done. This sequence defeats voice cloning because it doesn't trust the inbound channel.

questions.stem: A communications team wants to reduce the impact of deepfake disinformation that targets the company's brand. Which measures help? Select TWO.
options: Use content provenance or watermarking on official media
Prepare a rapid-response plan to publicly rebut false content
Rely on employees to notice lip-sync errors
questions.explain: Provenance and watermarking let audiences verify genuine media, and a rebuttal plan limits the spread of fakes. Going silent isn't practical and doesn't stop fakes, and visual cues get less reliable as models improve.

questions.stem: In a generative adversarial network, which component tries to distinguish real samples from synthetic ones?
questions.explain: The discriminator classifies samples as real or generated, while the generator creates the samples. Encoders and tokenizers belong to other architectures and are not the GAN's judging role.

questions.stem: A company's ML malware classifier is being bypassed by samples that appear tuned to score as benign. Which defensive measure BEST improves the model's robustness?
options: Adversarial training with perturbed and synthetic examples
questions.explain: Adversarial training exposes the model to evasive examples so it learns to resist them. Verbose output and published thresholds help attackers tune their samples, and removing logs reduces visibility.

questions.stem: For each statement about adversarial networks and security, select Yes if true.

statements.s: GANs can be used to generate realistic synthetic faces for fake online identities.
Allowing unlimited, unmonitored queries to a detection model makes it easier for an adversary to tune evasive inputs.
Adding a single additional ML detector removes the need for any other security layer.

questions.explain: GANs produce realistic synthetic media, and unlimited queries let a detector serve as an oracle, so rate limits and monitoring help. No single detector replaces defense in depth.

questions.stem: Which type of reconnaissance gathers information from public sources without interacting with the target's systems?
questions.explain: Passive reconnaissance uses public sources (OSINT) with no direct contact. Active reconnaissance and credentialed scanning interact with systems, and fuzzing sends malformed input to applications.

questions.stem: A CISO worries that attackers are using AI to analyze the company's job postings, staff profiles and public repositories. Which action BEST reduces this risk?
options: Add IDS signatures for OSINT tools
Perform regular OSINT self-assessments and remove unnecessary public detail
Block search engines at the firewall
questions.explain: Passive AI reconnaissance never touches your network, so the fix is reducing and reviewing your public footprint. IDS signatures can't see it, blocking outbound search engines doesn't stop outsiders, and password length doesn't affect OSINT.

questions.stem: Which controls help defend against AI-accelerated reconnaissance? Select THREE.
options: External attack surface management to find exposed assets
Secret scanning on public code repositories
Rate limiting and WAF rules to slow automated enumeration
Publishing detailed network diagrams for transparency
questions.explain: EASM finds what attackers can see, secret scanning removes leaked keys, and rate limits and WAF rules slow active probing. Publishing diagrams helps attackers, and disabling logs blinds defenders.

questions.stem: Phishing simulations show staff now click flawless, personalized AI-written lures. Which update to awareness training is MOST appropriate?
options: Teach staff to look mainly for spelling and grammar errors
Train staff to trust messages that mention real colleagues
Remove phishing training because AI messages are undetectable
Focus on suspicious requests, such as urgency, secrecy and credential or payment changes, and on reporting
questions.explain: AI removes language errors and adds real context, so training must focus on the request and the reporting path. The grammar cues are outdated, real names prove nothing, and dropping training increases risk.

questions.stem: Which authentication control BEST limits the damage when an AI-crafted phishing page captures a user's password and one-time code?
options: Phishing-resistant MFA such as FIDO2 security keys or passkeys
questions.explain: FIDO2 and passkeys are bound to the legitimate site's origin, so credentials relayed through a fake page fail. SMS codes and security questions can be phished or relayed, and expiry periods don't stop real-time theft.

questions.stem: An attacker uses an AI-cloned voice of a manager in a phone call to persuade staff to share information. Which social engineering type is this?
questions.explain: Voice-based social engineering is vishing, and AI voice cloning makes it more convincing. Smishing uses SMS, whaling targets senior executives (the caller here only poses as a manager), and tailgating is physical entry.

questions.case: Accounts payable receives an email thread that appears to continue a real conversation with a supplier. It names the correct invoice numbers and contacts and asks for future payments to go to new bank details. The language is flawless and the sender domain differs from the supplier's by one character.
questions.stem: Which control would MOST reliably have prevented a fraudulent payment?
options: A keyword filter for the word "urgent"
A policy requiring verification of bank-detail changes through a known supplier contact
A spelling and grammar checker on inbound mail
questions.explain: Out-of-band verification of payment changes defeats the scheme however convincing the email is. Keyword and grammar checks fail against fluent AI text, and archiving doesn't prevent the payment. Lookalike-domain detection would also help.

questions.stem: A SOC sees thousands of malicious scripts, each with a unique hash, that all behave the same way when executed. Which detection approach is MOST effective?
options: Adding every new hash to a blocklist
Behavior-based detection with EDR and sandbox detonation
questions.explain: Polymorphic, AI-generated variants defeat hash and name matching, but their behavior stays the same. EDR and sandbox detonation detect what the code does. Hash lists and definition updates always lag behind new variants.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY goal of obfuscation in an attack?
options: To speed up execution of the code
To disguise malicious content so analysis and detection fail
To compress files for faster delivery
questions.explain: Obfuscation hides intent from defenders while keeping function the same. Speed and compression aren't its purpose, and ransom encryption is a different action.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI and obfuscation, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An LLM can help analysts explain or de-obfuscate a suspicious script during triage.
Analysts should run unknown samples on production endpoints to see what they do.
Runtime script inspection, such as AMSI, can reveal script content after it is decoded.

questions.explain: AI can speed up de-obfuscation, and AMSI-style inspection sees decoded script content. Unknown samples belong in an isolated sandbox, never on production systems.

questions.stem: An attacker's AI combines an engineer's public commit history, conference bio, photo metadata and a breached personal password into a detailed target profile. Which concept does this BEST illustrate?
questions.explain: Linking scattered, individually harmless data into a sensitive profile is automated correlation, or aggregation. Model inversion extracts training data from a model, augmentation expands training data, and tokenization substitutes data values.

questions.stem: Which controls reduce the effectiveness of AI-driven data correlation against an organization's staff? Select THREE.
options: Strip metadata from published images and documents
Screen new passwords against known-breached password lists
Apply data minimization to what is published and retained
Publish full staff directories with phone numbers
Reuse the same username format across all public services
questions.explain: Removing metadata, blocking breached or reused passwords, and minimizing data all deny attackers raw material. Full directories and consistent public usernames make correlation easier.

questions.case: A research team released a de-identified data set of customer purchase histories, with names removed. A journalist used AI to match purchase times and store locations with public social media check-ins, then identified dozens of customers.
questions.stem: What is the BEST lesson for future releases?
options: Removing names alone is sufficient anonymization
Only release data in encrypted form to the public
Treat combined quasi-identifiers as sensitive and use anonymization that resists linkage, or release less detail
Ban journalists from accessing published data
questions.explain: Correlation across sources enables re-identification through quasi-identifiers such as time and location, so they need generalization or minimization. Removing names is insufficient, public encrypted data is useless to readers, and restricting journalists doesn't stop other attackers.

questions.stem: Threat reports warn that AI-assisted tooling is shrinking the time between a vulnerability's public disclosure and its exploitation. Which defensive change is MOST appropriate?
options: Move to quarterly patching to reduce change risk
Prioritize risk-based patching of known-exploited, internet-facing vulnerabilities
Rely solely on the vendor to notify you of attacks
Disable vulnerability scanning to avoid alert fatigue
questions.explain: Faster exploitation calls for faster, risk-prioritized patching of exposed, known-exploited flaws. Quarterly patching widens the window, depending on vendor notices is passive, and turning off scanning removes visibility.

questions.stem: In attack terminology, what is a payload?
options: The network path used to reach a target
The part of an attack that performs the malicious action once delivered
questions.explain: A payload is the component that carries out the harmful action. The path to the target is the attack vector, and reports and firewall rules are defensive artifacts.

questions.stem: Generative AI is lowering the skill needed to produce malware variants. Which defensive measures MOST directly limit the impact? Select TWO.
options: Application allowlisting and least privilege on endpoints
Relying only on static file hashes
Granting all users local administrator rights for productivity
questions.explain: Allowlisting and least privilege limit what any code can run or do, and behavior-based EDR catches new variants. Static hashes miss variants, and local admin rights widen the impact.

questions.case: A mid-sized company reads that criminals use AI to rank exposed services and misconfigurations across the internet within hours. It has no inventory of its internet-facing assets, and several cloud storage buckets were created by individual teams without review.
questions.stem: What should the security team do FIRST?
options: Implement external attack surface management to discover and assess internet-facing assets
Begin an awareness campaign about voice phishing
questions.explain: You can't defend assets you don't know about. Discovering and assessing exposed assets is the direct answer to AI-driven attack vector discovery. Deepfake tools and vishing training address other vectors, and honeypots help detection but don't remove exposures.

questions.stem: Why are honeypot alerts considered high-fidelity?
options: Legitimate users have no reason to interact with them, so any interaction is suspicious
They replace the need for a SIEM
questions.explain: Decoys have no business purpose, so any touch signals likely malicious activity. Honeypots don't block or encrypt traffic, and they feed a SIEM rather than replacing it.

questions.stem: A web service is hit by a distributed flood whose requests use realistic browser headers and human-like timing from thousands of residential IP addresses. Which defense is MOST effective?
options: Static blocklist of a few source IP addresses
Disabling TLS to reduce server load
Behavioral bot management with ML traffic baselining and a cloud scrubbing service
questions.explain: Adaptive, human-like DDoS traffic needs behavioral analysis and upstream scrubbing. Static IP blocks fail against thousands of rotating sources, disabling TLS harms security, and verbose logging adds load without mitigating.

questions.stem: For each statement about honeypots, DDoS and AI, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Generative AI can help defenders build more realistic decoy content for honeypots.
A honeypot is primarily a preventive control that stops attacks from reaching production.
Unusually expensive prompts sent at volume can cause model denial of service against an AI application.

questions.explain: AI improves decoy realism, and costly prompts can exhaust AI resources (model DoS). Honeypots mainly detect and gather intelligence. They don't prevent attacks on production.

questions.stem: Users find a lookalike download site for a popular AI coding assistant that installs a malicious extension. Which control BEST protects the organization?
options: Allow users to install any extension that has good reviews
Rely on users to compare logos
Allow only approved extensions from verified sources through managed policy
questions.explain: A managed allowlist of verified, sanctioned extensions blocks malicious lookalikes. Reviews can be faked, logo checks are unreliable, and turning off logging removes detection.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes low-code from no-code platforms?
options: Low-code allows optional custom code alongside visual components, while no-code requires none
Low-code platforms are always open source
No-code platforms run only on premises
questions.explain: Low-code combines visual building with optional scripting, and no-code is purely visual configuration. Both commonly use connectors, and neither is defined by licensing or hosting model.

questions.stem: A SOC analyst used a no-code platform's AI to build a workflow that reads the shared phishing mailbox. The workflow's connector uses a global administrator account. What should be changed before production?
options: Nothing, because the platform is approved
Use a dedicated least-privilege account scoped to the mailbox, and review the flow
Share the admin credentials with the whole SOC for support
Convert the flow to a personal assistant
questions.explain: Connectors should use least-privilege, dedicated credentials, and flows need review before go-live. An approved platform doesn't make broad credentials safe, sharing admin credentials worsens the risk, and switching to a personal assistant doesn't fix the access issue.

questions.stem: Which governance controls are appropriate for citizen-developed, AI-generated low-code automations? Select THREE.
options: DLP policies restricting which connectors can share data
Peer review and testing in non-production before deployment
Version control and change records for flows
Allowing any personal account connector to production data
Skipping review because AI generated the logic
questions.explain: DLP on connectors, peer review with testing, and versioning bring automations under control. Personal connectors to production data and skipping review on AI-generated logic increase risk.

questions.stem: A low-code workflow has a script step that redacts email addresses from alert text before sending it to an external LLM. Complete the code.
questions.explain: re.sub(pattern, repl, string) replaces every match with the replacement text, which redacts the addresses. re.match only tests the start of the string, findall returns the matches without replacing them, and compile doesn't take these arguments this way.

questions.stem: An AI combines the incident timeline, chat transcripts and ticket notes into a new post-incident report. Which task is this?
questions.explain: Combining several sources into a new document is synthesis. Augmentation expands training data, tokenization splits text or substitutes values, and signature matching is detection.

questions.stem: A company deploys a RAG assistant that writes audit summaries from internal documents. A junior employee's summary includes figures from an HR investigation file they can't normally open. What is the MOST likely design flaw?
options: The model's temperature is too low
Retrieval doesn't enforce the requesting user's document permissions
The prompt template is too short
questions.explain: RAG retrieval must be permission-aware, so it only returns documents the requester is allowed to see. Temperature, template length and translation don't cause unauthorized data exposure.

questions.stem: For each statement about automating document synthesis, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Requiring the AI to cite source records makes it easier for reviewers to check facts.
An AI-generated regulatory report can be filed without human review if it uses a prompt template.
Secrets and personal data should be redacted before content is sent to an external model.

questions.explain: Citations help verification, and redaction prevents leakage. A template standardizes format but doesn't prevent hallucinations, so a human must still approve official reports.

questions.stem: Which technique standardizes the structure of AI-generated incident reports, such as an executive summary, timeline, root cause and actions?
questions.explain: A prompt template fixes the input structure and the expected output format. Pruning and quantization shrink models, and rate limiting controls request volume.

questions.stem: A SOC receives 300 alerts in ten minutes, all tied to the same compromised account. Which AI ticket automation MOST directly reduces analyst workload?
options: Deduplicating and merging related alerts into one incident ticket
Creating a separate ticket for each alert
Automatically closing all alerts from that account
Emailing every alert to the CISO
questions.explain: Correlating and merging related alerts into one incident cuts noise and alert fatigue. A ticket per alert adds noise, auto-closing hides a real compromise, and mass email overloads leadership.

questions.stem: An AI ticketing system classifies an alert as a false positive with 55% confidence. The alert involves a domain controller. What should the system do?
options: Route it to a human analyst for review
Downgrade it to the lowest priority and archive it
questions.explain: Low-confidence decisions on critical assets belong with a human. Auto-closing or archiving risks missing a real attack, and deleting logs destroys evidence.

questions.stem: Put the AI-assisted incident ticket workflow steps in order.
options: Create ticket from alert and merge duplicates
Enrich with context and route to the right team
AI drafts closure summary and lessons learned
questions.explain: Tickets are created and deduplicated, then classified, enriched and routed. A human handles containment, and AI drafts the closure documentation at the end.

questions.stem: A SOC manager wants to show that AI ticket automation shortened the time from detection to resolution. Which metric should be tracked?
questions.explain: MTTR measures the average time to respond to or resolve incidents. RPO is about acceptable data loss, MTBF is about reliability, and ALE is a risk cost estimate.

questions.stem: An organization wants AI to speed up change approvals without weakening control. Which design is MOST appropriate?
options: AI auto-approves all changes it scores as low risk, including emergency database schema changes
AI approves changes submitted by senior engineers without review
AI replaces the CAB for all change types
AI auto-approves only pre-authorized standard changes and gives risk analysis to human approvers for normal changes
questions.explain: Standard changes are pre-authorized and suitable for automation, while normal and high-risk changes keep accountable human approval informed by AI analysis. The other options remove oversight or bypass separation of duties.

questions.stem: During a canary deployment, error rates on the new version jump above the agreed threshold. What should an automated pipeline do?
options: Automatically roll back to the last known-good version and alert the team
Promote the release to all users to dilute the errors
Disable monitoring until the release completes
Wait for the next CAB meeting
questions.explain: Objective health-check failure should trigger automated rollback and notification. Promoting spreads the failure, disabling monitoring hides it, and waiting prolongs the impact.

questions.stem: Which prerequisites make automated rollback reliable? Select TWO.
options: A tested rollback plan with defined health thresholds
Deleting previous releases after each deployment
questions.explain: You can only roll back to a version you kept, and a tested plan with objective thresholds lets the rollback trigger automatically. Deleting old releases prevents rollback, and weekly manual checks are too slow.

questions.case: An engineer submits a change to modify production firewall rules. The AI change assistant notes the request has no backout plan, conflicts with a scheduled network maintenance window, and resembles a past change that caused an outage. The engineer asks to approve it personally to save time.
questions.stem: What is the BEST outcome?
options: Let the engineer approve their own change because AI already reviewed it
Auto-approve the change since firewall changes are routine
Return the change for a backout plan and reschedule, then escalate for human approval with the AI risk findings
Deploy immediately and rely on monitoring
questions.explain: The AI found missing information, a conflict and historical risk, so the change needs completion and accountable human approval. Self-approval breaks separation of duties, and auto-approval or immediate deployment ignores the identified risk.

questions.stem: What MOST distinguishes an AI agent from a basic chatbot?
options: It uses a larger context window
It autonomously plans and takes actions through tools toward a goal
It only answers questions from a knowledge base
It never connects to external systems
questions.explain: Agents act: they plan, call tools, observe the results and iterate. Context size doesn't define an agent, answering from a knowledge base is chatbot behavior, and agents usually do connect to external systems.

questions.stem: A SOC deploys an AI triage agent. Which configuration BEST balances automation with safety?
options: Domain admin rights so the agent never fails
Full autonomy to delete suspicious accounts
Read-only tool access by default, with human approval required before containment actions
questions.explain: Least privilege plus human-in-the-loop for high-impact actions limits excessive agency. Admin rights and autonomous deletion are excessive, and removing logs prevents audit.

questions.case: An AI agent summarizes reported phishing emails and can create firewall block rules. After processing one reported email, the agent tried to add an allow rule for an unknown external IP. The email body contained hidden text telling the agent to allow that address.
questions.stem: Which control would have BEST prevented the agent from acting on this?
options: Restrict the agent to an allowlist of actions (block only) and require approval for firewall changes
Let the agent process emails faster
questions.explain: This is indirect prompt injection that exploits excessive agency. Allowlisted actions and approval gates stop injected instructions from taking effect. A bigger context window, more speed or a larger model doesn't remove the permission problem.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI agents in security operations, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Each plan step, tool call and result an agent makes should be logged for audit.
Data an agent reads, such as emails or logs, can contain instructions that manipulate it.
Giving an agent broad permissions reduces the risk of excessive agency.

questions.explain: Logging gives accountability, and indirect prompt injection arrives through processed data. Broad permissions are the cause of excessive agency, not a fix for it.

questions.stem: Which pipeline check identifies known vulnerabilities in open-source libraries that an application depends on?
questions.explain: SCA inventories third-party components and matches them to known CVEs and licences. SAST checks your own source code, DAST tests the running app, and unit tests verify functions.

questions.stem: Which are appropriate uses of AI in CI/CD code scanning? Select TWO.
options: Explaining findings to developers and proposing fixes for review
Prioritizing findings by whether the vulnerable code is reachable
Automatically merging AI fixes to production without tests or review
Disabling security gates when the backlog grows
questions.explain: AI adds value by explaining, suggesting fixes and prioritizing by reachability. Fixes still need review and tests, and disabling gates removes the control.

questions.stem: A developer accidentally commits a cloud access key. Which pipeline control should catch this before merge?
questions.explain: Secret scanning detects credentials in commits and can block the merge. Regression and model tests verify behavior, and canary deployment happens after merge, at release.

questions.stem: A bug fixed last quarter reappears after a new feature is merged. Which test type was designed to catch this?
options: Unit testing of the new feature only
questions.explain: Regression tests re-run existing checks to confirm earlier behavior and fixes still hold. Testing only the new feature misses old paths, and pentests and load tests target other concerns.

questions.stem: Before promoting a retrained LLM-based classifier to production, which model tests should the pipeline run? Select THREE.
options: Accuracy against a held-out validation set compared with the current baseline
A suite of known prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts
Bias and fairness checks across user groups
Checking that the model file name follows naming standards only
questions.explain: Model testing covers performance against a baseline, robustness and guardrail safety, and fairness. File naming and developer metrics don't evaluate the model.

questions.case: A retrained spam-detection model passes all unit and regression tests and is deployed automatically. Within an hour, production monitoring shows recall falling sharply and user reports of missed phishing rising. The previous model version, its prompts and its data set snapshot are stored in the model registry.
questions.stem: What is the BEST immediate action, and what should be improved?
options: Keep the new model and retrain overnight; add more unit tests
Disable spam filtering; skip testing next time
Roll back to the previous model version, then add a model-testing gate that compares recall against the baseline
Lower the alert threshold on monitoring; remove the registry
questions.explain: Rolling back to the versioned known-good model restores protection at once, and a baseline-comparison model test would have blocked the release. Keeping a degraded model or disabling filtering exposes users, and removing the registry prevents future rollbacks.

questions.stem: Put the secure CI/CD pipeline stages for an AI-enabled application in order.
options: Run code scanning and SCA on the commit
Build and run unit and regression tests
Run model testing against baseline and guardrail suites
Deploy to a canary group with health monitoring
Promote, or automatically roll back if health checks fail
questions.explain: Scans run first on the commit, then build and functional tests, then model evaluation, then a staged deployment with monitoring, ending in promotion or automated rollback.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of an AI Center of Excellence (CoE)?
options: To monitor production AI workloads for intrusions around the clock
To set AI strategy, standards and reusable practices and coordinate governance across the organization
To act as the external auditor that certifies the organization's AI systems
To replace business-unit teams so that all AI solutions are built by one central group
questions.explain: A CoE is a cross-functional hub that sets strategy, standards, reference patterns and governance. Round-the-clock intrusion monitoring is the SOC's job. External certification needs an independent body. CoEs usually enable business units (hub-and-spoke) rather than replacing them.

questions.case: A retailer's marketing, HR and logistics departments have each signed separate contracts with different generative AI vendors. Security finds three different prompt-logging approaches, no shared guardrails and no single list of AI systems in use. The CIO wants consistent controls and reuse without stopping innovation in the departments.
questions.stem: Which action BEST addresses the CIO's goals?
options: Require each department to hire its own AI auditor
Block all generative AI vendors until a single vendor is chosen
Move all AI budgets into the security operations center
Establish an AI Center of Excellence with an executive sponsor to set standards, approve use cases and maintain an AI inventory
questions.explain: A sponsored CoE gives one set of standards, a shared guardrail pattern, intake approval and an AI inventory, while departments keep building (hub-and-spoke). A blanket block stops innovation. Separate auditors per department don't create common standards. The SOC is not a governance or strategy body.

questions.stem: A document gives step-by-step instructions for submitting a new AI use case, completing the risk questionnaire and obtaining sign-off. What type of governance document is this?
questions.explain: Step-by-step 'how to' instructions are a procedure. A policy states high-level intent and requirements. A standard sets mandatory specifics that support a policy. A guideline is optional recommended practice.

questions.stem: An organization's AI use-case approval procedure is being documented. Put the steps in order.
options: Business owner submits the use-case request with purpose and data involved
Use case is risk-classified using the AI risk policy
Governance board reviews the assessment and approves, rejects or adds conditions
Approved system is recorded in the AI inventory with an accountable owner
System is monitored and periodically re-reviewed
questions.explain: Intake comes first, then risk classification so reviewers know what level of scrutiny applies. The board decides on that evidence, approved systems are registered in the inventory with an owner, and ongoing monitoring and re-review follow deployment.

questions.stem: Which role is PRIMARILY responsible for building ingestion pipelines, enforcing data quality checks and recording data lineage for training datasets?
questions.explain: Data engineers design and run pipelines, quality checks and lineage capture. Data scientists consume the curated data to train and evaluate models. AI risk analysts assess risks. AI auditors independently review controls; they don't build pipelines.

questions.stem: A team member explores historical claims data, engineers features, compares several algorithms and evaluates them with precision and recall. Which role does this describe?
questions.explain: Exploring data, feature engineering, training and evaluating candidate models is the data scientist's core work. Platform engineers provide compute and tooling. MLOps engineers automate deployment and monitoring. AI governance engineers implement governance controls.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI roles, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A machine learning engineer typically turns a validated model into robust, optimized production code and serving APIs.
A platform engineer is mainly responsible for choosing features and tuning model hyperparameters.
An AI architect designs how a model, data sources such as a vector store, and applications fit together end to end.

questions.explain: ML engineers productionize models; AI architects design the end-to-end solution. Feature selection and hyperparameter tuning belong to data scientists (and ML engineers); platform engineers build and run the compute and tooling platform.

questions.stem: A company needs someone to build pipelines that retrain models on new data, store each version in a model registry, run canary deployments and automatically roll back when drift thresholds are breached. Which role BEST fits?
questions.explain: Automated retraining, model registry and versioning, deployment strategies, drift monitoring and automated rollback are MLOps responsibilities. Data engineers own data pipelines, not model release pipelines. AI architects design solutions. AI risk analysts assess risk rather than build automation.

questions.stem: The audit committee wants an independent assessment of whether the company's AI systems comply with internal policy and the EU AI Act. Which role should perform it?
questions.explain: Independent evaluation of controls and compliance, reported to leadership or the audit committee, is the AI auditor's role. The security architect and governance engineer design and build the controls, so they lack independence to audit them. MLOps engineers run release pipelines.
